newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-PEN PICS OF U.S. RYDER CUP TEAM.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-PEN PICS OF U.S. RYDER CUP TEAM.

text.p: Brief profiles of the 12 members of the U.S. Ryder Cup team that will try to take back the cup from Europe next month at Valderrama in Spain:
-- Fred Couples - A talented and versatile player who has been a mainstay of four U.S. teams, Couples is a captain's selection for the second consecutive time.

Other notable achievements: Winner of the 1992 Masters and 11 other tour events, he has ranked seventh or better in scoring on U.S. tour in five of the past six years; was joint seventh in this year's Masters and British Open.

-- Lee Janzen - While Janzen, a captain's selection like Couples, lost his only two Ryder Cup matches at The Belfry in 1993 (in four-ball and singles), both came down to the final hole with the match tied.

Other notable achievements: Winner of the 1993 U.S. Open and six other tour events, Janzen impressed captain Tom Kite with his fine play in the PGA Championship, where he was fourth, one of only four players to break par for the championship.
-- Tiger Woods - Playing professionally for less than a year, Woods won six tour events, including this year's Masters, and accumulated the most points (1,185) to qualify for the team.
Other notable achievements: Became youngest Masters champion in April, winning with a record score and by a record margin; won unprecedented three consecutive U.S. Amateur championships.
-- Justin Leonard - One of golf's emerging young stars, Leonard finished second to Davis Love in PGA Championship to finish second in points earned (1,068).

Other notable achievements: won the British Open in July for his first major title and second victory of the year; a protege of Byron Nelson, he won the 1992 U.S. Amateur and 1994 U.S. college championship.
-- Tom Lehman - After toiling for years on minitours, Lehman is now one of the best in the game, leading the PGA Tour last year in scoring average and earnings.
Other notable achievements: Won 1996 British Open; second and third in last two U.S. Opens; beat Seve Ballesteros 4 and 3 in '95 Ryder Cup singles.
-- Davis Love - Won PGA Championship on Sunday for his first major title; son of a famous teaching professional, he was a steady player on the last two cup teams.
Other notable achievements: Winner of 11 tour events, he has eight top-10 finishes this year, including joint 10th at the British Open; second in 1996 U.S. Open and 1995 Masters.
-- Jim Furyk - Another under-30 star, despite an unorthodox swing, finished tied for sixth at the PGA Championship for his 12th top-10 finish of the season.
Other notable achievements: Won tour events in 1995 and 1996; ranked first in putting on tour in 1995; finished fourth in this year's British Open.
-- Phil Mickelson - Only undefeated player in 1995 matches as rookie, winning his singles match and two four-ball matches with different partners, has won 11 tournaments on U.S. tour.
Other notable achievements: first golfer since Jack Nicklaus to win 10 U.S. tour events by age 26; won four times last year and twice this year, including Sprint International two weeks ago.

-- Jeff Maggert - Finished third in PGA Championship to win a place in last opportunity for a second time, his joint third in 1995 PGA at Riviera got him on that team; helped U.S. take Ryder lead in '95 matches with first-day victories in both foursome and two-ball matches with different partners.
Other notable achievements: Has one victory (in 1993) on tour; five top-10 finishes this year, including two seconds and a fourth at U.S. Open.
-- Mark O'Meara - The second oldest of the 10 players who won automatic berths and most experienced member of a very young team.
Other notable achievements: Winner of 14 events in 17 years on tour, including back-to-back victories early this year; ranked second in putting and fifth in earnings on tour last year.
-- Brad Faxon - One of the better putters in the game, he ranked first in tour putting last year, when he finished eighth in earnings -- without a victory.
Other notable achievements: He shot 63 in final round of 1995 PGA Championship at Riviera Country Club to make his first Ryder Cup team.
-- Scott Hoch - Perhaps best known for missing a two-foot winning putt in a playoff with Nick Faldo in the 1989 Masters, he has seven victories on U.S. tour and one in Europe.

Other notable achievements: Lost to Greg Norman in final of Andersen Consulting World Championship in January; ranked ninth in earnings and 11th in scoring on tour last year; has seven top-10 finishes this year.
